title: The Gnedenko-Kolmogorov Domain of Attraction Theorem
description: When does the Central Limit Theorem generalize beyond finite variance? The Gnedenko-Kolmogorov theorem gives a complete characterization: a distribution lies in the domain of attraction of an α-stable law if and only if its tails are regularly varying with index -α. This file formalizes slowly varying functions, regular variation, the tail balance condition, and states the full forward, converse, and Gaussian cases of the theorem.

mathlibDependencies.description: Real power function for defining regular variation

sections.title: Slowly Varying Functions
sections.description: Defines slowly varying functions L(x) satisfying L(cx)/L(x) → 1 as x → ∞. Proves closure under multiplication and power operations.

sections.title: Regular Variation
sections.description: Defines regularly varying functions f(cx)/f(x) → c^α and connects to slowly varying (α=0 case). States that x^α is regularly varying.

sections.title: Tail Balance Condition
sections.description: Formalizes the tail balance structure: right and left tails decay as x^{-α}·L(x) with weights p and q determining the skewness of the stable limit.

sections.title: Domain of Attraction
sections.description: Defines InDomainOfAttraction via characteristic function convergence: φ^n(t/aₙ)·exp(-ibₙt/aₙ) → exp(-|t|^α).

sections.title: The Gnedenko-Kolmogorov Theorem
sections.description: States the full theorem: forward direction (tail conditions → domain of attraction), Gaussian case (finite variance → α=2), and converse (domain of attraction → regular tail variation).

sections.title: Properties and Connections
sections.description: Potter's bound for slowly varying functions, Karamata's integral theorem, stable self-similarity, and the connection between classical CLT and Gaussian domain of attraction.

sections.title: Concrete Tail Balance Instances
sections.description: Constructs TailBalance instances for the one-sided Pareto distribution (p=1, q=0) and symmetric Cauchy distribution (p=q=1/2), connecting abstract tail theory to concrete distributions.

sections.title: Domain of Attraction for Concrete Distributions
sections.description: Uses the axiomatized forward direction to show Pareto (0<α<2) and symmetric Cauchy distributions lie in the domain of attraction of their respective α-stable laws.

sections.title: Slowly Varying Function Examples
sections.description: Proves log(x+a) is slowly varying for a≥1 and |log(x+a)|^β is slowly varying for any β≠0, providing non-constant examples of slowly varying functions.

overview.summary: The Central Limit Theorem tells us that sums of iid random variables with finite variance converge to a Gaussian. But what happens when variance is infinite? The Gnedenko-Kolmogorov theorem provides the complete answer: a distribution lies in the domain of attraction of an α-stable law (0 < α ≤ 2) if and only if its tails are regularly varying with index -α. This file builds the framework of slowly varying and regularly varying functions, defines the domain of attraction via characteristic functions, and states all three parts of the theorem.
keyIdeas: Slowly varying functions L(x) satisfy L(cx)/L(x) → 1 and serve as correction factors in tail asymptotics
Regular variation f(cx)/f(x) → c^α generalizes power-law behavior
The tail balance condition p/(p+q) determines the skewness parameter of the limiting stable law
The Gnedenko-Kolmogorov theorem gives a complete iff characterization for domains of attraction
The classical CLT (α=2) is a special case where variance is finite and L is constant

conclusion.summary: Formalizes the framework for understanding when the CLT generalizes beyond finite variance, culminating in the statement of the Gnedenko-Kolmogorov domain of attraction theorem with forward, converse, and Gaussian cases.
openQuestions: Full proof of the forward direction requires Lévy's continuity theorem and Karamata theory
The converse requires Abelian-Tauberian theory connecting char fn convergence to tail behavior
